metadata.description: Language-agnostic workflow plugins for Claude Code — cross-model AI collaboration, rebase automation, changelog generation, and TDD workflows

plugins.name: weave
plugins.description: Run independent adversarial participants through host-native sub-agents by default or separate model CLIs by choice — brainstorm, refine, plan, execute, architect, review, and synthesize

plugins.name: rebase
plugins.description: Automated rebase onto trunk with conflict prediction, resolution, and quality gate verification

plugins.name: changelog
plugins.description: Generate categorized changelog entries from branch commits and PR context; refresh or recut a branch's own entries as it evolves

plugins.name: tdd
plugins.description: TDD bug-fix workflow — reproduce bugs as failing tests, find root cause, fix, and verify

plugins.name: commit
plugins.description: Create git commits following project conventions with format enforcement and safety checks

plugins.name: model-cli
plugins.description: Run prompts through individual AI CLIs — Antigravity/agy (Gemini), codex/GPT, and cursor/agent with fallback support

plugins.name: pr
plugins.description: Generate, refresh, recut, and review gold-standard PR descriptions; detect AI slop, brittle counts, and verbose commit messages on branch commits and resolve via fixup commits and autosquash with quality-gate checks

plugins.name: research
plugins.description: Clone and study your project's dependencies at the exact versions you use — source repos with version-pinned git worktrees

plugins.name: slop
plugins.description: Scan repo tracked files for AI slop, brittle counts, and verbose noise; resolve each finding as an atomic forward-going commit with quality-gate verification

plugins.name: tailwind
plugins.description: Detect and fix inconsistent spacing in Tailwind CSS layouts — container fragmentation, margin/gap mixing, padding asymmetry, and more

plugins.name: pytest-optimizer
plugins.description: Profile a pytest suite, rank safe speedups with a safety-first rubric, and apply each as its own verified commit

plugins.name: spike
plugins.description: Prove a path fast in a no-commit spike — a single probe or a bakeoff of competing strategies in git worktrees — exit through the project's quality gates into stashes, and hand back a commit-by-commit implementation plan

plugins.name: review
plugins.description: Address code-review findings on the current branch — provenance-gated to changes the branch introduced, one finding per commit, simplest pragmatic fix, with quality gates before every commit and prompted history rewrites

plugins.name: action
plugins.description: Take tickets to branches in isolated git worktrees — resolve Linear/GitHub issues strictly read-only, name branches by the team's own conventions, land gated commits, and fan out multiple tickets in parallel

plugins.name: lean
plugins.description: Write tight, slop-free prose and code, and tighten existing files in place with no commits — a model-invocable writing discipline plus a working-tree cleanup command

plugins.name: double-check
plugins.description: Make verification requests return the re-derived answer instead of a diff against the agent's prior turn — an ambient skill for 'double check' / 'are you sure' moments plus an /align command to repair a chat where the diff already happened

plugins.name: release
plugins.description: Cut and bump releases with safe defaults — no push, no tag, no tag push without an explicit flag — and roll new releases out to every downstream consumer repo with CI verification

plugins.name: merge-pr
plugins.description: Merge PRs via gh with merge commits matching the repo's own git history — readiness checks and CI watch before every merge, plus multi-PR runs with stack detection, rebase, and conflict resolution between merges

plugins.name: business
plugins.description: Measure and report the business value of AI skills and agentic workflows — provenance-tagged data collection and audience-tiered reports in engineer-hours and cycle time, never currency

plugins.name: github-actions
plugins.description: Update GitHub Actions pins across one repo or a whole fleet — verify every target tag exists before writing it, research each upgrade against real release notes, land one commit per action on trunk, then close dependabot's PRs by citing the commit that superseded them

plugins.name: situate
plugins.description: Gain situational awareness before touching a repository — sweep the branch against trunk, its diff, its pull request and review threads, its linked tickets, and the project's own conventions, optionally searching prior AI conversations for decisions the repository never recorded; answer a mid-session 'huh' in five lines or less; and re-derive what the work is for to catch both the work nobody asked for and the work nobody did

plugins.name: terraform
plugins.description: Move Terraform and OpenTofu versions across any repository layout — discover every root module instead of assuming one, move every declaration of a provider together because constraints combine across modules, and refresh each lock file without narrowing its platform coverage

plugins.name: ruff
plugins.description: Move one repo or a whole fleet onto a new ruff release — work out which rules the release can actually fire against each repo's own select list, gate on the resolver being able to see the version at all, then land one reviewed commit per rule with the upstream rule doc cited

plugins.name: gh
plugins.description: File GitHub issues a maintainer can still act on in three years — evidence and reproduction before prose, duplicates and the repo's own templates checked first, every symbol backticked and every source link pinned to a tag or a commit, long output folded into details blocks, local paths and PII stripped before anything is opened — plus the rendered-markdown writing discipline those bodies follow, reusable for any pull request, comment, or ticket a renderer will show a human

plugins.name: git-branch
plugins.description: Redo a branch two ways — keep the code and rebuild only the history into atomic commits, proving the resulting tree is byte-identical to what it replaced; or keep the requirements and replace the implementation from scratch, holding the branch's own tests as the specification and reconciling the result against a ledger of everything the original handled. Both draw their commit messages from the original commits, the pull request, its tickets, and the session that wrote the code, gate every commit through the project's own checks, and never push on their own — plus an editor-free interactive-rebase toolkit for reordering, squashing, and verifying history from an agent shell with no TTY

plugins.name: package-updater
plugins.description: Update dependencies and toolchain pins across one repo or a whole fleet — check the supply-chain cooldown before calling anything current, then land the toolchain, the named bumps, the bulk lockfile refresh and their fallout as separate commits, each with the upstream release notes cited
